sentences.text: The holotype, the specimen the species is based on, is a partial skeleton of a subadult that includes vertebrae, a scapula, pelvic fragments, leg bones, and partial foot bones, but lacks any skull traces.
Erliansaurus was a small to medium-sized therizinosaur estimated to be between 2.6 and 4 meters long and weighing between 91 and 400 kilograms.
This animal was a bipedal herbivore.

The specific name bellamanus means "beautiful hand" in Latin, referencing the exquisite preservation of the forelimb which features enormous, strongly recurved and pointed claws, with the thumb claw being the largest.
Fossils of Erliansaurus were discovered near Sanhangobi in Inner Mongolia in 1999.
The type species Erliansaurus bellamanus was described by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2002.
The holotype specimen, LH V0002, comes from the Santonian stage of the Iren Dabasu Formation.
The original describers assigned Erliansaurus to Therizinosauroidea in a basal position, suggesting it was likely not a therizinosaurid.
However, some early cladistic analyses recovered Erliansaurus as a basal member of the Therizinosauridae.
The Paleobi Database classifies Erliansaurus within the family Therizinosauridae.
Fossil evidence places Erliansaurus in the Campanian stage, ranging from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
